Who controls the answer?. A NOTIFICATION appeared on some iPhones carrying the BBC News logo. Luigi Mangione, the man accused of killing UnitedHealthcare chief executive Brian Thompson in New York, had shot himself, it said. Except he had not. Mangione was alive and in custody. The BBC had published no such claim. Apple Intelligence grouped three BBC notifications into a single summary and turned one into a false statement. Following complaints from the BBC and other news organisations, Apple temporarily suspended notification summaries for news and entertainment apps. The incident was widely treated as another AI error, but its implications went further. The BBC had done the reporting, yet AI had changed what potentially millions of users thought it had reported. Its name remained on the alert even though it no longer controlled the information attached to it. Something similar is now happening on a much larger scale. People are turning to AI assistants with questions they once asked Google, journalists or experts, such as what happened in an election or why a war began. In all fairness, search engines were never neutral to begin with. They decided whether a report from Dawn appeared beside an obscure Indian website presenting itself as a research platform, and most users rarely moved beyond the first few results. But users could still open the original reports, see where each claim came from and judge the sources. AI removes that step. It reads the material, summarises it and presents its own version of what happened. This matters because malicious actors are already polluting the information space. Elections bring coordinated disinformation, synthetic audio and manipulated videos designed to promote candidates or discredit opponents. Governments and parties are no longer simply responding to news but producing their own version of events. People are turning to AI assistants with questions they once asked Google, journalists or experts, such as what happened in an election or why a war began. The same contest is visible in Gaza, where restrictions on journalists, competing claims and loaded language have shaped coverage. The killing of civilians, destruction of hospitals and homes, restrictions on aid and wider Israeli abuses are extensively documented, yet presented through radically different frames. Months of reporting by journalists, UN agencies and human rights groups may be placed against a single denial from the Israeli or US government. An AI assistant may then present both as equally credible, without showing how much evidence supports each account. The history of occupation may disappear, leaving what appears to be a dispute between two sides. The democratic danger is not limited to hallucination. It lies in allowing a handful of private companies to organise public knowledge. Citizens may receive one answer without knowing which newsroom established the facts, what evidence supports them or which accounts were left out. A confident summary can close a debate before the reader knows one exists. This is already happening. A study coordinated by the European Broadcasting Union and led by the BBC examined more than 3,000 responses from four major AI assistants across 18 countries and 14 languages. It found that 45 per cent had at least one significant issue. Serious sourcing problems appeared in 31pc, while 20pc contained major accuracy issues. There is an economic consequence too. Traditional search normally preserved the click. Readers reached the news website, encountered the original reporting and generated some advertising or subscription value. AI systems can extract the result of that work, compress it into a paragraph and retain the user. Pew found that users were almost half as likely to click on a search result when an AI summary appeared. Publishers surveyed by the Reuters Institute expect search traffic to fall by 43pc over the next three years. Their reporting is still being used, but fewer readers are reaching the organisations that produced it. Large international publishers are negotiating licensing agreements with AI companies but smaller organisations have little comparable leverage. This is particularly dangerous for Pakistan, where journalism is already weakened by declining revenues, political pressure, delayed salaries and dependence on government and corporate advertising. Most publishers have no subscription base, limited technical capacity and little understanding of how often AI systems collect their work. The European Union has begun addressing parts of the problem. Its AI Act requires certain AI-generated or manipulated material, including deepfakes and unedited text on matters of public interest, to be labelled. Providers of general-purpose AI models must maintain copyright compliance policies and publish summaries of their training material. Systems designed to influence elections are treated as high risk, while the Digital Services Act requires the largest platforms and search engines to address risks to elections and civic discourse. But these protections do not settle the central question. They do not require an assistant to present several credible accounts, explain why it preferred one source, direct users prominently to the original report or compensate the publisher whose journalism supplied the answer. Pakistan needs to begin this discussion before the terms are set elsewhere. News organisations should measure AI crawling and referral traffic, decide how their archives may be used and bargain collectively with technology companies. Common agreements should require clear attribution, links to original reports, a process for correcting false summaries and fair payment when journalism is used commercially. Publishers must also rebuild direct relationships with audiences through memberships, newsletters and products that do not depend entirely on platforms. Journalism has lost audiences to new technologies before. This time, AI does not only decide which report is seen. It can rewrite the report, mix it with weaker sources and deliver the result without the reader reaching the newsroom. If these systems depend on reporting, they cannot be allowed to make the reporter disappear. The writer is the founder of Media Matters for Democracy. Published in Dawn, August 26th, 2026

Pakistan Agricultural Research Council suspends officers over ‘recruitment irregularities’. ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Agricultural Research Council (PARC) has suspended several officers over their alleged involvement in irregularities in the organisation’s recruitment process, senior officials of the Ministry of National Food Security and Research informed a Senate committee on Tuesday. The officials told the Senate Standing Committee on National Food Security and Research that an inquiry under the Efficiency and Disciplinary Rules had also been initiated against the officers. The committee was further informed that the matter was currently sub judice. The meeting, chaired by Senator Syed Masroor Ahsan, was attended by Senator Poonjo Bheel and Senator Sardar Al Haj Muhammad Umer Gorgaij. The committee expressed serious concern over the failure to submit the required written reply and relevant record concerning the alleged recruitment irregularities. Members also discussed the plight of candidates who had applied for PARC vacancies but were now approaching the upper age limit. The committee recommended exploring a mechanism that would allow such candidates to participate in future PARC recruitment drives even if they subsequently exceed the prescribed age limit, in order to protect their interests. Members also stressed that the prescribed provincial quota must be implemented across all posts, including lower-grade positions. Officials said the required codal formalities for implementing the provincial quota had been completed and assured the committee that the quota would be enforced. The committee was also briefed on the National Oilseed Policy and the country’s growing edible oil import bill. Officials said the federal government was planning measures to increase domestic oilseed production, with particular emphasis on olive cultivation. Senator Ahsan expressed concern over the challenges confronting domestic edible oil production and called for practical steps to boost local output. He directed the ministry to submit a comprehensive report covering progress made over the past three years, PSDP projects, initiatives related to olive oil production and future plans to increase domestic oilseed production.­ Published in Dawn, August 26th, 2026

Israeli MP smashes West Bank memorial under army escort. • Tel Aviv begins evicting UN training centre for Palestinians • West Bank settlers attack journalists, activists near Bethlehem RAMALLAH: A far-right Israeli lawmaker took a sledgehammer to a Palestinian memorial in the occupied West Bank on Tuesday while under military escort. Footage circulating on­­line showed Zvi Sukkot, who is also a settler and activist, smashing a monument commemorating “martyrs” in the Pales­ti­nian village of Madama in the northern West Bank, while soldiers stood nearby. “A few days ago, I demanded that the military take action to remove the monuments commemorating ter­­rorists in the murderers’ villages of Madama and Burin. Unfortu­na­tely, they remained in place. So, I went there myself and took action to re­­m­ove them,” Sukkot posted on Face­book, along with a video of the act. The Israeli military said Sukkot and his aides had conducted a “tour” of the area “with security provided by IDF soldiers who had been diverted from their operational activities for this purpose”. “Contrary to the agreed-upon coordination, the participants acted deceptively and manipulatively, without authorisation, departing entirely from the appr­o­ved framework, and began demolishing one of the monuments in Madama,” it added. It said soldiers reported the incident to their commanders, who told them to stop the activity and “the participants were quickly escorted out of the village”. In a statement, Prime Minister Benjamin Netan­yahu said the military “is the sovereign authority in Judea and Samaria”, using the Biblical term for the occupied West Bank. “Taking the law into one’s own hands, especially when it involves public figures, is a reprehensible practice that prevents the IDF from focusing on its missions of combatting terrorism and incitement to violence,” he added. Israel raids UNRWA training centre Meanwhile, Israeli for­ces began evicting a vocational training centre run by the UN agency for Palestinian refugees in an east Jerusalem suburb on Tuesday, in its latest move targeting the beleaguered organisation. It follows repeated warnings by UNRWA that Israeli authorities were threatening its Qalandia training centre, located between the east Jerusalem neighbourhood of Kafr Aqab and the Qalandia refugee camp. The centre was established in 1952 and offers vocational training to around 340 Palestinians from the occupied West Bank every year, according to UNRWA. (left) Zvi Sukkot, a member of the Israeli Knesset, smashes a monument at Madama, in the occupied West Bank; while (right) journalists react after inhaling tear gas during a raid by Israeli forces on a UN-run vocational training centre near Ramallah.—AFP “In accordance with my directive and following the law we passed, today the evacuation of the UNRWA compound in Kafr Aqab in Jerusalem has begun,” a statement from Netanyahu’s office said. Israel has repeatedly accused UNRWA of providing cover for Hamas fighters, claiming that some of its employees took part in the group’s Oct 7, 2023 attack. Israel’s far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben Gvir, on Tuesday celebrated “making history!” “Large forces of the Israel police are operating together with the relevant bodies to implement the law and remove UNRWA from the site,” he said on Telegram. He later posted a photo of the Israeli flag hoisted above the entrance to the training centre with the caption: “UNRWA in our hands.” An AFP journalist at the scene on Tuesday said Israeli forces had closed the main road near the entrance to the Qalandia Training Centre, while forces inside the institute were moving from one building to another. The journalist reported seeing a convoy of three civilian vehicles leaving the institute, escorted by Israeli forces. West Bank settlers attack journalists Separately, Israeli settlers in the West Bank on Tuesday attacked journalists reporting on tension with Palestinians, in violence that left at least five people injured, the reporters and medics said. A three-person team from the AFP news agency had travelled to the village of Jannatah near Bethlehem to report on Israeli activists who conduct solidarity visits with Palestinians facing harassment by Israeli settlers, who recently blocked a road in the area. After an altercation broke out between the settlers and activists, the Israeli military ordered journalists to leave what it called a “closed military zone”, at which point two additional cars full of settlers swooped in. The settlers, many of them children, threw stones towards the journalists and activists. One journalist ducked a stone but then a child settler struck him in the chin with a stick, causing minor bleeding, he said. The AFP journalists returned to see their two parked cars both damaged, with back windshields smashed in and tyres punctured. Published in Dawn, August 26th, 2026

Deaths in Township police custody: Forensic report confirms women were addicts: IGP. LAHORE: Punjab Inspector General of Police (IGP) Abdul Kareem says the forensic report of the two young women, who had died in Township police station, has confirmed that they had been using addictive drugs or prohibited substances. Addressing a press conference here on Tuesday, along with other senior officers of Lahore police, he said the forensic report was prepared by a medical board comprising senior doctors. The IGP said that according to the report, both young women died of cardiopulmonary arrest, an acute medical emergency where the heart suddenly stops pumping blood and breathing ceases. He said the report also revealed that the women were using nine kinds of intoxicating substances which led to their death during interrogation in the police custody. To a question, the IGP said that though death of the two women at the same time was unusual, the forensic reports have made it clear that they died of addictive substance. About the progress in the investigation into Hina Javed’s murder case registered in Rawalpindi, the IGP said that three suspects were nominated in the FIR and two of them have been arrested by the police. The victim was found dead in the washroom of her apartment in a housing scheme in Rawalpindi on Thursday evening. The police said the body bore signs of torture, with a wire around the neck and it was tied to the shower rod. The IGP said the Rawalpindi police handled the case professionally by proving during investigations that it was a murder, not a suicide case. The investigations into the Hina Javed’s murder case are underway and the police will soon bring the culprits to the court of law, he added. Talking about the murder of Abdullah Tahir, a PTI ticket-holder from Okara, he said the shooters who targeted the victim fled to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab police teams are working on the case to trace and arrest them as soon as possible. On Eid Miladun Nabi, PM Shehbaz and President Zardari urge nation to follow teachings of the Holy Prophet. President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday urged the nation to draw guidance from the life and the teachings of the Holy Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) and make hard work and service to humanity the purpose of their lives, state-run Radio Pakistan reported. In separate messages on Eid Miladun Nabi, both leaders extended heartfelt felicitations to the nation and the Muslim Ummah on the birth anniversary of Holy Prophet (PBUH). In his message, the president said, “It is incumbent upon us to practically promote justice and fairness, tolerance, inter-sectarian and interfaith harmony, and the protection of human dignity in our society. “This day reminds us of the great blessing of Allah Almighty through which humanity was granted the perfect path of faith, guidance, justice, mercy and noble character,” he added. Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz said that in order to overcome the economic, social and moral challenges confronting the country, “we must mould our collective lives in accordance with the perfect guidance provided by Islam”, the state broadcaster reported. The prime minister called for playing a role in making Pakistan a strong, prosperous, peaceful and welfare state. In a separate post on X, he said that the life and teachings of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) “remain an eternal source of guidance for all humanity — calling us towards compassion, justice, tolerance, unity and service to others”. “Let us pledge to illuminate our character and collective conduct with the light of Seeratun Nabi and work together for a peaceful, and prosperous Pakistan,” he said. Muslims around the world celebrate the birth of Prophet Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Him) on the 12th of Rabiul Awwal — the third month of the Islamic lunar calendar.

'A privilege, not a right': US to revoke visas of up to 200,000 asylum seekers. The US government plans to revoke the visas of foreigners who came to the country for tourism or business but sought to stay longer by applying for asylum, the State Department said on Tuesday. The crackdown marks another step in the Trump administration’s signature drive to reduce immigration into the United States. The administration said it is now working with the Department of Homeland Security to identify and revoke the visas of people who, it said, came to America billing themselves as temporary visitors but then applied for asylum so they could stay permanently. “Obtaining a visa in order to seek asylum is fraud — which is grounds for visa revocation,” State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a statement that confirmed press reports about the new policy. The White House, in a post on X, suggested “up to two hundred thousand visas” would be affected and claimed it would be the “largest mass visa revocation in history”. The State Department neither confirmed nor denied that number. Pigott said, “The number of revocations remains dynamic and will be done on a rolling basis.” Early this month, the department said that since President Donald Trump returned to power in January 2025, some 175,000 foreigners had seen their US visas revoked on grounds ranging from criminal offenses, including driving under the influence, to praising the killing of the right-wing activist Charlie Kirk. The administration also recently revoked the visas of Mexican officials, including the son of the former president Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador. This prompted a complaint from the current president, Claudia Sheinbaum. Trump, who won reelection in large part on his promise to fight illegal immigration, has expelled huge numbers of people who were in the country without proper residence papers. But he has also worked to restrict the entry of foreigners who do go by the rules and has gone after those who overstay their visas after they expire. Some of these measures have been challenged and curtailed by the courts. Last Friday a federal judge struck down a government ban on visas to nationals from 75 countries who wish to settle in the country indefinitely. These countries included Afghanistan, Brazil, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Somalia, Thailand and Yemen. The Trump administration is also planning to expand vetting of the social media accounts of visa applicants. “We are making clear that a visa is a privilege — not a right,” Pigott said on Tuesday.

Mayor Mamdani opposes NYC event with leader of India's Hindu nationalist group. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Tuesday he did not support an upcoming event in his city featuring the leader of the Hindu nationalist group that is the ideological parent of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Mohan Bhagwat, chief of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), is scheduled to speak at a Manhattan event on Saturday, according to the event’s website. “I don’t support the rally, but I don’t know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event,” Mamdani, who is the first Muslim and Indian American mayor of New York City, said when asked if the event should be cancelled. “The vision of India that I was taught by my family and one that I grew up being very familiar with was of a pluralistic society of a secular Republic that believed in the belonging of each and every person who was from India. And it has been incredibly troubling to see the rise of a movement that is predicated on an exclusionary vision.” The event’s website casts the August 29 gathering as the “Universal Oneness Celebration” bringing together the Hindu American community. The organisers, American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue, say the event is backed by several Hindu American groups and promotes shared heritage and interfaith unity. Many local organisations have criticised it over Bhagwat’s attendance and the RSS’ history. The RSS, a powerful Hindu group from which Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP emerged, said in May it had organised foreign visits, including to the US, to counter perceptions it is a paramilitary outfit involved in attacks on minority communities. The US Commission on International Religious Freedom says the RSS “has been involved in acts of extreme violence and intolerance against members of minority groups for decades”. The RSS disputes intolerance accusations and says it is a “Hindu-centric civilisational, cultural movement” whose goal is to “carry the nation to the pinnacle of glory”, including by uniting Hindus. United Nations and human rights groups say abuse of Indian minorities has risen in recent years, pointing to rising hate speeches , a religion-based citizenship law , the demolition of Muslim-owned properties, the removal of occupied Kashmir’s autonomy and an anti-conversion legislation that challenges freedom of belief. The BJP-led Indian government denies being discriminatory and says its policies, including food subsidy programmes and electrification drives, benefit all communities.

14 infants killed in fire at Pims' gynae ward in Islamabad. ISLAMABAD: Fourteen infants were killed in a fire that broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) early on Wednesday. Footage aired on television showed rescue workers using ladders to reach broken windows to access the affected area. Outside the hospital, an AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the medical facility. In a statement, the Islamabad administration said that the fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward. It said that rescue teams rushed to the scene, with six fire brigade vehicles and four ambulances taking part in the rescue operation. “The fire was immediately brought under control and the children were immediately shifted to the intensive care unit,” it said, adding that 14 children “were completely burnt”. Pims Spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn that 15 babies were in the ward. “At least one baby was saved by a doctor,” she said. Speaking to Geo News , Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said that the infants in the ward were either in incubators or on oxygen. He said the incident occurred at 6:45am due to a “blast in the air conditioner” inside the ward. He said that the blast caused the fire, which was exacerbated due to the presence of the oxygen tanks. He confirmed that 14 infants had been killed, adding that law enforcement agencies were on the ground. Malik Israr, whose niece was admitted to the gynae ward, told Dawn that it was unfortunate the nursery was housed in a building in which repair and renovation work was ongoing. “After the fire erupted, they told patients to vacate the building. Women who had just given birth had to rush down the stairs from the second floor,” he said. Pims, established in 1985, is Islamabad’s biggest public sector hospital. It is one of two of the oldest health facilities in the federal capital and comprises several hospitals and teaching institutes. Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement. Inquiry committee formed A notification issued by the Islamabad district magistrate said that a fact-finding committee, headed by the additional deputy commissioner general, had been formed to determine the facts behind the fire. The members of the committee included the director general of the Capital Emergency Services, the City police station superintendent, the assistant commissioner (Industrial Area), the director general of the Capital Development Authority’s Electrical and Mechanical wing, representatives from Pims and Islamabad Electric Supply Company. The committee was tasked with determining the exact cause of the fire, assessing whether adequate and functional fire-safety measures were in place, and evaluating the response time and effectiveness of the rescue and fire-fighting operations. The notification said that a report would be furnished within 24 hours. Ambulances are parked outside a mortuary following a deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP PM takes notice Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to investigate the incident. According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), he expressed deep sorrow and grief at the incident and offered his condolences to the bereaved families. “Such a situation involving children is unbearable,” the statement quoted him as saying. “The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken,” he said. President Zardari expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families. In a statement, the president said that the loss of lives was “heartbreaking and an irreparable loss”. “Responsibility for the incident should be determined and action should be taken in accordance with the law,” he said. Effective fire safety and emergency arrangements must be ensured in hospitals for the protection of patients, especially newborn babies, the president urged. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said the loss of innocent lives was an unbearable tragedy for the entire nation and expressed heartfelt sympathy and solidarity with the bereaved families. He called for an impartial investigation into the incident and said that the nation be informed how such a tragedy occurred at a major hospital. “Those responsible for negligence or failing to ensure the safety of patients must be held accountable,” he added, stressing that the federal government must ensure the safety of patients and medical staff at all hospitals under its administration. Senate Chairman Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani expressed deep grief and sorrow over the tragic incident. In a statement, he offered his condolences to the families affected. He said effective safety measures, fire safety systems and all necessary arrangements to deal with emergencies must be ensured in hospitals to prevent such incidents. “Any negligence in safety measures is unacceptable,” he said. Gilani urged the relevant authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident and take effective and practical steps to prevent such tragedies in the future. National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq also expressed profound grief and sorrow over the deaths of the infants. In a statement, he said he was “heartbroken” over the incident and shared equally in the pain and grief of the bereaved parents. The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) said in a statement that it was in “deep mourning” over the incident. “The association reiterates that healthcare facilities are designed to protect and restore human lives, yet administrative failure and regulatory oversight lapses have turned these institutions into danger zones,” it said. It demanded action against officials “whose failure to uphold safety codes resulted in this catastrophe”. It also demanded enforcing strict consequences so that “systemic failure serves as a decisive warning, preventing future lapses across both public and private medical facilities”. It further said that there should be immediate restructuring and public accountability of health regulatory authorities responsible for enforcing safety protocols, building codes and emergency infrastructure in hospitals. The PMA also called for “full institutional backing for the grieving parents, ensuring they receive complete legal, financial, and emotional justice”. Additional input from AFP

AboitizPower, ZANECO renovate Tinglan Child Development Center. Aboitiz Power Corporation (AboitizPower) and Aboitiz Foundation Inc. partnered with the Zamboanga del Norte Electric Cooperative (ZANECO) to renovate the Tinglan Child Development Center in Barangay Tinglan, Mutia, providing about 30 local children with a safer and brighter learning space. The initiative is the seventh completed project under the AboitizPower Revenue Operations group’s Adopt-a-Daycare Program and covers structural repairs, as well as the donation of new furniture and school supplies. Coinciding with the turnover was the signing of an Emergency Power Supply Agreement (EPSA) for two megawatts between AboitizPower and ZANECO, with Therma South Inc. helping supply the latter’s service area in Zamboanga del Norte. “Guided by our purpose to Transform Energy for a Better World, we work together with ZANECO to create an inspiring environment where young learners can grow, explore, and dream big,” said AboitizPower Head of Revenue Operations James Yu. "This project reflects what our partnership with AboitizPower is truly about. They haven't just been a power provider to ZANECO — they've been a true partner, going beyond powering businesses and communities to help make projects like this possible,” explained ZANECO General Manager Atty. Jordanne Chan-Antonio. “That matters most when it comes to our children, who are at the heart of every community we serve." The corporate social responsibility initiative builds on an 11-year relationship between AboitizPower and ZANECO through Therma South Inc. For more than a decade, the two organizations have supported the local economy and power stability of Zamboanga del Norte. “Ngayon, mas ligtas at komportable na ang daycare namin para sa mga bata. Dito na sila pwedeng mag-aral at maglaro nang maayos,” added Ginalyn Ferrancullo, Daycare Teacher at Tinglan Child Development Center. “Sobrang pasasalamat namin sa AboitizPower at ZANECO. Talagang nakikita namin ang pagmamahal nila para sa aming komunidad.” (Today, our daycare is safer and more comfortable for the children. Here they can study and play properly. We are deeply grateful to AboitizPower and ZANECO. We can truly see their love for our community).

Megaworld targets 12,000 hotel rooms by 2032, names new hospitality execs. Andrew Tan-led top township developer Megaworld Corp. is ramping up the expansion of its hospitality business, targeting 12,000 rooms by 2032 after setting its sights on some of the Philippines’ fastest-growing tourism destinations. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Wednesday, Aug. 26, Megaworld said it is rolling out new hotel developments in key destinations, such as Palawan and Ilocos Norte provinces, alongside continued expansion in major tourism and business hubs across the country. This expansion will include both Megaworld’s homegrown hotel brands and international brands, further strengthening the company’s position as the Philippines’ biggest developer and operator of hotel developments. Apart from opening more hotels, Megaworld is also reshaping its hospitality business to prepare for a bigger and more global hospitality sector. To drive this next phase of growth, Megaworld has established Megaworld Global Hotels and Resorts (MGHR) to bring together its growing hotel portfolio under two focused groups. First is Megaworld Hotels & Resorts (MHR), which will manage the company’s hotel developments in Metro Manila, Boracay, Batangas, and Cebu. Then there is Megaworld Global Hospitality (MGH), which will handle Mövenpick Manila Bay Westside, Megaworld’s biggest hotel property, as well as the company’s new hotel properties in Palawan and three hotels in Iloilo province: Courtyard by Marriott, Richmonde Hotel Iloilo, and Belmont Hotel Iloilo. “One of our biggest contributions to nation-building is to help make our tourism industry more vibrant and attractive, especially to foreign visitors,” said Megaworld President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Lourdes Gutierrez-Alfonso. To support this goal of helping boost the country’s tourism sector, she said, “we are making this bold move of expanding our hospitality organization with established veterans and innovators in the global hotels and leisure industry.” “We see tourism as one of the most powerful engines of sustainable economic growth. Every hotel we build creates jobs, supports local businesses, brings visitors to new destinations, and opens more opportunities for communities to prosper,” said Kevin L. Tan, president and CEO of Alliance Global Group Inc. (AGI), the parent company of Megaworld. He noted that “Through our expanding hospitality portfolio under MGHR, we want to help continue unlocking the immense tourism potential of the Philippines and bring more of our country’s destinations, culture, and world-class Filipino hospitality to travelers from around the globe.” In line with this, the two Megaworld hospitality groups will be led by seasoned industry executives: Socrates Alvaro, who will be the managing director of MHR, and Anna Vergara, who is taking the helm as managing director of MGH. Alvaro brings extensive hotel operations and leadership experience, with a distinguished track record built through various senior leadership roles within MHR. His career spans nearly two decades across some of the world’s most dynamic and prestigious hospitality markets, including the United Kingdom (UK), United Arab Emirates (UAE), Egypt, the Maldives, Thailand, and other key destinations across Asia. Vergara, meanwhile, brings more than 32 years of distinguished experience with Marriott International, the world’s largest international hotel chain. She has built a reputation for excellence in hotel operations, leadership, and the development of high-performing teams. Together, Alvaro and Vergara bring complementary strengths to the new organization—one anchored on Megaworld’s homegrown hospitality expertise and the other on global hotel standards and international brand management. For the first half of 2026, Megaworld’s hospitality business emerged as the company’s fastest-growing recurring income segment, delivering an 11-percent increase in revenues to ₱3.1 billion. The strong performance was fueled by the opening of the 405-room Belmont Hotel Iloilo, the company’s third hotel within its 72-hectare (ha) Iloilo Business Park and now the largest hotel in Iloilo City in terms of room inventory, bringing Megaworld’s total hotel portfolio in the city to nearly 1,000 rooms. - James A. Loyola

How a Chinese film shot in dialect is finding a global audience. BANGKOK (AP) — The buzziest film in China this year was shot almost entirely in a southern Chinese dialect that most Chinese viewers need subtitles to understand. Yet “Dear You” has become China’s second-highest-grossing film of the year. Now it is heading overseas, part of a broader wave of Chinese cultural exports. “Dear You” was shot mostly in Teochew, a dialect spoken in Guangdong’s Shantou region. Set among the Teochew immigrant community in Bangkok, it tells the story of people who left China in search of work to support their families. Made on a low budget, it features a cast of mostly unknown actors. The film provides a glimpse into the centuries-long history of Chinese migration to Southeast Asia. It has succeeded in making this little-discussed history visible to a wider audience while meeting official censorship requirements and telling a compelling story, experts say. As of August, the movie had grossed about 269 million yuan ($40 million) at the Chinese box office. It was released in Thailand in early August after being shown in Singapore, Malaysia and Australia. It will be released in the U.S. next month. China is increasing its soft power with cultural exports The film’s popularity comes as Chinese culture and consumer brands have been gaining global attention, from Labubu dolls to “Chinamaxxing,” a social media trend embracing aspects of the Chinese lifestyle. The Chinese government began promoting the film as it became a hit and prepared for its international release. The Chinese consul in Sydney said at a June screening of the film that it “reflects the Chinese nation’s virtues of diligence, kindness, courage and unity.” The movie aligns with Beijing’s broader goal of “telling China’s stories well,” highlighting themes of friendship, tradition and family, including motherhood and kinship, said Belinda He, an assistant professor of East Asian cinema and media studies at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. China’s ambassador to Thailand presented the film at a special screening in July and again at a red carpet event this month. “We’re grateful to Guangdong for making such a wonderful film,” Chinese ambassador Zhang Jiangwei said at the red carpet event, which was attended by officials from Guangdong’s Information Office. “Stories about ordinary people and simple, genuine emotions can be even more moving. This film is an excellent vehicle for telling China’s story well.” Chinese migration to Southeast Asia has been ongoing for centuries The film first resonated in Malaysia and Singapore because it showcases a history that’s rarely featured in mainstream films. Chinese migration to Southeast Asia dates back centuries, with many migrants coming from the Guangdong and Fujian provinces in southern China. Many worked as laborers in building projects during an era of Western colonial rule across much of Asia. The film starts with a young man trying to find his grandfather, Deng Musheng, in hopes of getting a loan to repay his debts. In the family lore, there was supposedly a wealthy grandfather in Thailand who left his young wife and children behind in China and never came back. Using an address on an old remittance letter his grandfather had sent, he meets people who became part of his grandfather’s life in Bangkok, uncovering the mystery of why his grandfather never returned. The film’s director, Lan Hongchun, wrote in a column for the People’s Daily, a state media outlet, that he grew up hearing stories from his grandmother about people she knew migrating to Bangkok and wanted to tell these stories in film. The film also resonates with Thai Chinese viewers The plot revolves around “qiaopi,” remittance letters used by Chinese immigrants to send money and news back home. Many workers who could not write Chinese relied on scribes to compose the letters. Scenes set in the centralized offices where the scribes worked, called “poy kuan,” were directly out of the childhood of 74-year-old Sathien Tuntipaiboontana. “I connected emotionally with that part of the film quite strongly,” he said after watching the first screening of the film in a Bangkok theater with his older sisters and sisters-in-law. Among them was his eldest sister, who is 89 and needed help climbing the stairs to the cinema. Their father had immigrated to Bangkok from China in search of work, leaving behind a wife and children. He ended up remarrying and never returned to China. But Sathien’s family continued to send remittances to the family left behind in China. Thitikorn Phanprayoon, a third-generation Thai Chinese, said he decided to see the film after hearing Teochew, the Chinese dialect he speaks at home, in the trailer. It surprised him since most Chinese films are in Mandarin. He plans to return with his parents. “I felt like I was sitting at home,” he said. “It felt like my family was performing in the movie in front of me.”

PAGASA monitoring cloud clusters for possible LPA development. Cloud clusters east of the country are being monitored for possible low-pressure area (LPA) development that could further enhance the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Wednesday, Aug. 26. PAGASA senior weather specialist Glaiza Escullar said the habagat remains the dominant weather system as of Wednesday. “We are also closely monitoring cloud clusters east of Northern Luzon, as well as far east of Visayas. So minomonitor po natin yan for the possible formation of LPAs within these cloud clusters dahil may effect din po yan sa enhancement ng habagat (We are also closely monitoring cloud clusters east of Northern Luzon, as well as far east of the Visayas. We are monitoring them for the possible formation of LPAs within these cloud clusters because they could also affect the enhancement of the southwest monsoon),” Escullar said during PAGASA’s climate forum. Escullar said Typhoon Saudel, formerly locally named “Obet,” which is currently crossing Japan, continues to stir the southwest monsoon. “Ito pa rin ang nagpapairal sa southwest monsoon dahilan para meron pa ring expected na habagat in the coming days (It is still driving the southwest monsoon, which is why the southwest monsoon is expected to continue in the coming days),” she said. Due to anticipated significant rainfall over parts of Luzon, PAGASA’s Weather Division has issued a heavy rainfall advisory for the next three days. On Wednesday, occasional rains of 50 to 100 millimeters, categorized as moderate to heavy, are expected to continue over Zambales. On Thursday, Aug. 27, occasional moderate to heavy rains are expected over La Union, Pangasinan, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan, and Occidental Mindoro. By Friday, Escullar said the effects of the enhanced habagat are expected to spread further, with occasional rains of 100 to 200 millimeters, classified as heavy to intense, forecast over Zambales and Occidental Mindoro. Occasional moderate to heavy rainfall are also expected over Metro Manila, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, and Batangas.

Man nabbed for stealing P12,000 auto parts in QC. A 25-year-old man was arrested early Tuesday morning, Aug. 25, after allegedly stealing P12,000 worth of auto parts from a garage in Barangay Payatas, Quezon City. Police identified the suspect as alias “Nard,” who entered the garage with a companion at about 3:20 a.m. and took several auto parts from the shop at the corner of San Lorenzo Ruiz and San Vicente streets. The shop owner witnessed the theft and immediately sought help from patrolling officers of the Payatas Bagong Silangan Police Station (PS 13). A brief chase followed, resulting in Nard’s arrest, while his companion escaped and remained at large. Recovered from Nard were two car alternators worth P3,000, an electric starter worth P1,000, and a radiator worth P8,000. Police records showed that Nard had previous cases, including alarms and scandals and a violation of Batas Pambansa Blg. 6 in 2023; violation of Presidential Decree No. 1602 or illegal gambling in 2024; and violations of Republic Act No. 9287 or the Anti-Illegal Numbers Games Act in 2025. Nard will face a theft complaint before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office, while police continue their follow-up operation to arrest his companion.

2027 national tax allotment seen reaching P1.4 trillion — Palace. The projected National Tax Allotment (NTA) for local government units is expected to reach P1.4 trillion nationwide in 2027, with Luzon local government units (LGUs) set to receive P676.9 billion, Malacañang said. In a press briefing on Wednesday, Aug. 26, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the projected 2027 NTA would represent an 11 percent increase from current levels, while the proposed Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) allocation would rise to P58.532578 billion from P57.872578 billion in 2026. The higher LGSF allocation, she added, is intended to give local governments more resources to address infrastructure and social development needs, including farm-to-market roads, water systems, health facilities, bridges, disaster-resilient community facilities, and assistance to marginalized groups. She, however, assured the public that the national government's responsibility does not end after funds are released. “Hindi po natatapos ang obligasyon ng national government matapos ibigay ang pondo dahil kinakailangan po itong ma-monitor kung lahat po ng naibibigay na tulong sa ating lokal na pamahalaan ay nagagamit sa tama at hindi po naaabuso ang pondo (The obligation of the national government does not end after the funds are given because it is necessary to monitor whether all assistance provided to local governments is properly used and the funds are not abused),” Castro said. Asked about the national government functions expected to be devolved to LGUs next year, Castro said national agencies would continue to monitor the implementation of programs supported by the funds. She cited the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) for infrastructure projects and the Department of Education (DepEd), Commission on Higher Education (CHED), and Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) for scholarship-related assistance. The government has also streamlined documentation requirements for these funds, allowing local chief executives to submit and track requests online through the Ugnayang Bayan portal. Castro said President Marcos decided to increase the LGSF after listening to the concerns and recommendations of local government leaders, including feedback that the fund had produced positive results. She cited the assessment of Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo, who she said had described the implementation of the LGSF as positive and noted its transparency and the clear identification of where the funds should go. Castro said the President heard that municipalities and other LGUs needed additional resources to meet the needs of their constituents. Meanwhile, Executive Secretary Ralph Recto urged local officials to ensure that public funds are used properly and for the benefit of their constituents. “Ang hiling lang namin sa inyo ay gamitin nang tama (Our only request is that you use it correctly),” he said during the distribution of Special Allotment Release Orders (SAROs) under the LGSF to municipalities during the League of Municipalities of the Philippines Luzon National Congress on Tuesday, Aug. 25. The event also featured the on-site distribution of SAROs for LGSF Financial Assistance to LGUs (FALGU), the Growth Equity Fund (GEF), and the Support to Barangay Development Program (SBDP) for municipalities in Luzon. “Gamitin nang maayos. At higit sa lahat, gamitin para sa tao ang pondo ng bayan (Use it properly, and, above all, use public funds for the people),” he added. Recto also said every barangay nationwide would receive a direct P200,000 allocation from the Presidential Socio-Civic Projects Fund, with half intended to assist five graduating college students and the other half for local development projects. The LGSF, he said, also supports social welfare and food security programs, including the Bagong Pilipinas Rice Program, which provides 10 kilograms of rice every two months to nearly 8 million families. He urged LGUs to use their NTA and LGSF allocations for climate adaptation, disaster preparedness, and solid waste management, stressing the importance of preventive measures in reducing future rehabilitation costs. “Hindi po kakumpitensya ng national government ang LGU. Magka-team tayo (The LGU is not a competitor of the national government. We are a team),” Recto said. “Kayo ang katuwang namin, kakampi namin, at kamay ng gobyerno sa bawat komunidad (You are our partners, allies, and the government's hands in every community),” he added.

Infra project planning requirements stricter now, Dizon tells House. The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) told House of Representatives members that it has tightened requirements for the planning infrastructure projects as part of reforms following the flood control projects corruption. DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon led the agency’s contignent in the House Wednesday, Aug. 26 as the Committee on Appropriations carried out the agency's budget briefing under the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP). In his presentation before the solons, Dizon said all projects included in the NEP must have an approved program of work and complete mandatory supporting documents. The NEP, worth P7.2 trillion for next year, is the precursor to the General Appropriations Bill (GAB) or proposed national budget. Dizon said these supporting documents include validated geotagged photos taken directly at the project site. The DPWH head honcho explained that in the past, some projects merely relied on “tabletop coordinates,” using maps or Google Maps instead of actual site visits. Now, Dizon said DPWH requires project engineers, district engineers, and planning engineers to personally visit sites and take photos with automatic location coordinates to prove field validation. Commission on Audit (COA) Chairperson Gamaliel Cordoba earlier stressed that geotagging is crucial in fraud audits, since auditors often struggle to locate projects and determine if they are ghost projects. P51-M notices of disallowance In an earlier House budget briefing Tuesday, Cordoba shared that COA issued a total of P158 billion in notices to the DPWH this year. According to him, P107.77 billion are notices of suspension while P51.27 billion are notices of disallowance. "Of course, iba’t iba na po ang stages nito ngayon dahil may appeal, etc. (these are in different stages because of appeals, etc.) but the total amounts issued for DPWH only for this year is already P150 billion," he told the appropriations panel. Cordoba says auditing could be strengthened if COA is provided with 146 additional pre-audit teams drawn from audit, technical, and administrative positions. He estimates that about P2.5 billion would be needed to fund the additional personnel and other expenses of these pre-audit teams. Cordoba emphasizes that more pre-audit teams would help detect and prevent questionable government spending more promptly. He also notes that additional resources for COA are essential to strengthen oversight of the use of public funds.

BIR orders ‘audit of auditors’ to eliminate flawed tax assessments. The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) is subjecting its tax investigators to a second tier of scrutiny, introducing a revalidation process to eliminate calculation errors and enforce legal compliance across all assessment issuances. BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza ordered the mandatory second-round reviews in Revenue Memorandum Order (RMO) 22-2026, dated Aug. 24. The directive applies sweeping quality-control oversight across all authorized investigating offices from localized revenue district offices to the national investigation division. “To reinforce accountability, promote uniformity, and uphold quality standards in tax examinations, all audit investigation reports and assessment issuances may be subject to a revalida, or ‘audit of auditors,’” Mendoza stated in RMO 22-2026. This review mechanism establishes tight internal checkpoints designed to prevent unchecked decisions by individual examiners. Under the order, the tax audit review division is required to carry out technical vetting of audit findings, computations, and assessment issuances—all of which remain subject to final approval by the commissioner. The division will dissect each case file to confirm that every deficiency assessment is precise and backed by solid legal foundations. Meanwhile, the performance evaluation division will support the process by monitoring and ensuring the quality of audit outputs, including compliance with procedures, timelines, documentation, and audit-trail standards. These offices will verify that investigators strictly log their progress on digital platforms to establish a trail that is “complete, accurate, and capable of independent verification.” Audit findings and recommendations will be submitted to the tax chief for approval. Cases involving revenue regions and district offices must be endorsed by the Deputy Commissioner for the Operations Group (DCIR-OG), while those involving the Large Taxpayers Service (LTS) and National Investigation Division require endorsements from the DCIR-Special Regulatory Group (DCIR-SRG) and DCIR-Legal Group (DCIR-LG), respectively. This multi-tiered approval hierarchy ensures that high-ranking tax officials remain directly involved in oversight, preventing fragmented decision-making. “The revalida shall serve as a quality assurance and compliance review mechanism to ensure that audit findings are factually and legally supported, due process requirements are observed, and assessments are free from material error or procedural defect,” the BIR said. The creation of the revalida framework forms part of the agency's broader effort to standardize tax audit processes. The BIR is shifting to a “system-assisted, risk-based taxpayer selection process” aimed at protecting taxpayers and curbing corruption. Under the new regime, cases will be assigned through an anonymized process that conceals taxpayers’ identities during selection and assignment to ensure impartiality. It also categorizes audits into mandatory and priority cases while strictly enforcing a single-instance audit framework to prevent duplicate investigations within the same taxable year. While most audits will be system-triggered, the BIR assured that businesses with tax exemptions or incentives will not face automatic audits, insulating compliant firms from arbitrary examinations. “Taxpayers enjoying tax exemptions or incentives shall not automatically be subjected to audit. Such cases shall be subject to risk-based evaluation and validation,” the BIR said. Officers who fall short of these guidelines face serious consequences, as breaches of the order’s provisions constitute grounds for “appropriate administrative sanctions.” “Any violation of the provisions of this order, including but not limited to improper case selection, unauthorized audit, [or] misclassification of audit cases... shall constitute a ground for the imposition of appropriate administrative sanctions, without prejudice to civil or criminal liability, where applicable,” the RMO reads.

'Ang Pinakamasarap Na Pares Sa Balat Ng Lupa': Silly, crass and a lot of fun. “Ang Pinakamasarap Na Pares Sa Balat Ng Lupa” is not for everybody. Some might find it too stupid for its own good. That said, if you surrender to its brand of comedy, there are enough laugh-out-loud moments to make it work. It belongs to the tradition of weed-induced adventures like “Up in Smoke,” “Pineapple Express,” “Harold & Kumar Go to White Castle” and “Half Baked,” movies where logic takes a back seat and the characters simply go with the flow. And that is exactly what you have to do here. Just go with it. The comedy can be crass and, at times, downright inane. But the timing and chemistry of Jerald Napoles and Pepe Herrera carry much of it. The supporting cast is equally game. Despite the title, the movie isn't really about pares. Yes, the brothers are looking for the best one because one of them wants a delicious serving before his supposed 24 hours on Earth are up. But beneath the silliness is a story about two estranged brothers. One wants to cook but can't, so he becomes a food critic vlogger. The other can cook but knows his pares isn't as good as the one made by their grandmother. Both are jealous of each other, and that jealousy has driven them apart. So, underneath all the stupid jokes and pares-hunting, it is a story about love and understanding. Those who enjoy the old-school comedy of Rene Requiestas, Redford White and Babalu will likely find something familiar here. Just don't overthink it. Now in cinemas.

Meralco retail arm expands reach in Bulacan with power supply agreement. MPower, the retail electricity unit of Manila Electric Co. (Meralco), has secured a supply deal with Big Ben Group to power its manufacturing facilities in Pulilan, Bulacan. In a statement on Wednesday, Aug. 26, MPower said the partnership would allow the power retailer to deliver a reliable and cost-competitive power supply to support the construction material producer’s manufacturing operations and long-term expansion goals. Big Ben Group is a manufacturer and supplier of ready-mix concrete, providing materials for various real estate and commercial infrastructure developments. Benjamin Eusebio, Big Ben’s director, highlighted the importance of integrating sustainable energy practices into their core operations to support growth. “Sustainability has to be embedded in how we operate and plan for the future. Partnering with MPower enables us to improve our energy management while supporting our long-term business and sustainability goals,” Eusebio said. Eusebio Pacifico Garcia, the company’s chairman, added that securing an efficient energy source is critical to maintaining operational continuity and delivering quality output to clients. “Energy reliability and cost efficiency are fundamental to how we operate and compete. Partnering with a trusted provider like MPower strengthens the foundation of our business and supports our long-term vision for growth and resilience,” Garcia stated. Redel Domingo, head of MPower, emphasized the supplier’s commitment to delivering tailored energy solutions that enhance operational resilience for its partners. “By ensuring a stable and reliable power supply, we help create the conditions for businesses to focus on what they do best and continue creating value for their customers and communities,” Domingo said. Launched in 2013, MPower is one of the leading retail electricity suppliers (RES) in the country, servicing commercial and industrial contestable customers. Under the Retail Competition and Open Access (RCOA) framework of the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA), distribution utilities (such as Meralco) and electric cooperatives are authorized to establish their own RES units. (Gabriell Christel Galang)

Davao City eyes centralized data center for AI, records. DAVAO CITY — The Davao City government is moving toward establishing a centralized data center to consolidate servers, strengthen cybersecurity, and eventually support artificial intelligence applications. City officials discussed cybersecurity, backup power, data migration, and a dedicated facility as the City Information Technology Center (CITC) prepared plans for centralized systems. Funding and the final site, however, remain undecided. Diosdado Lopez, acting network head of the CITC, told the City Council that the government currently operates 17 to 19 server rooms spread across different offices. The proposed data center would centralize these servers, making them easier to manage. “There is no budget yet because we are still looking for the site,” Lopez said during deliberations on Tuesday, Aug. 25, at the Sangguniang Panlungsod. Several offices now maintain their own servers, with some systems linked for data sharing. Lopez described the setup as a hybrid network using both local and online connections. He said taxpayer records and civil registry data -- including birth, marriage, and death records -- require stronger protection. The city council raised concerns about risks tied to consolidating government information in one facility, citing cyber attacks, equipment failures, fires, and earthquakes. CITC officials assured members that redundancy measures, including external backups, are in place. Councilor Bonz Andrei Militar, chair of the Committee on Information Technology, proposed building a high-security facility rather than simply adding servers inside City Hall. The center could eventually house data on agriculture, land, disaster management, and other operations. Lopez noted that an earlier ICT building plan under the previous administration did not push through. A government project at People’s Park is now being considered for revision into a multi-story ICT facility. Power reliability was also raised, with CITC officials saying the proposed center would include uninterruptible power supply, standby generators, and possibly solar power with battery storage. Councilor Lorenzo Villafuerte suggested requiring redundant emergency power systems, which CITC agreed to. The facility would also feature precision cooling, restricted entry, biometric or facial-recognition access, CCTV, and fire and earthquake protection. Council members asked CITC to prepare for greater AI use, which Lopez said would require stronger GPUs and advanced cooling, making operations costly. Still, the council said AI could aid policymaking and government services. Existing servers could be integrated via application programming interfaces to minimize disruption during migration. The council also stressed the need for personnel skilled in data center management, cybersecurity, cloud computing, and disaster recovery. CITC currently employs trained staff and contractual cybersecurity specialists but is pursuing conversion into a regular city department. Council members recommended creating permanent technical positions given the sensitive nature of the data. The proposal remains under consideration, with funding, site selection, and design still to be finalized.

Quezon repels Pasay; Pasig overcomes Manila. Quezon Province leaned on Judel Fuentes to thwart Pasay, 67-59, on Tuesday, Aug. 25, and move closer to South division pacesetter Batangas City in the SportsPlus MPBL (Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League) 2026 Season at the Pasay Astrodome. Fuentes fired 25 points, including 14 in the fourth quarter, to power the Quezon Huskers to a 15-3 record in the round-robin elimination phase of the two-division, 26-team tournament. The Huskers, triggered by Fuentes' three straight triples, surged ahead, 62-51. The Voyagers' Rence Alcoriza answered with three charities, but Fuentes finished the demolition job by scoring Quezon's last five points against a fallaway jumper by Cyril Gonzales and a triple by Mark Parks. Fuentes also grabbed 4 rebounds and issued 2 assists to earn the SportsPlus best player honors over Cedric Manzano, who finished with 10 points, 12 rebounds, 2 assists and 2 blocks. "Finally, after two years, we won over them (Voyagers)," said Fuentes, a member of the South selection for the SportsPlus MPBL 2026 All-Stars on Saturday at Ynares Center Montalban in Rizal Province. Clint Escamis, a prized acquisition from the Mapua Cardinals, contributed 8 points, 4 rebounds and 2 steals for the Huskers, the reigning back-to-back South division champions. Pasay tumbled to 12-11 in the North division as only Rence Alcoriza found his range with 18 points and 7 rebounds. Steve Nash Enriquez accounted for 9 points and 2 rebounds, but Christian Fajarito, the Voyagers' Top Gun, was held to 4 points, 7 rebounds and 2 blocks. Pasig subdues Manila Pasig City hit full throttle in the fourth quarter and subdued Manila Batang Quiapo, 108-99, in the opener to remain in contention for an outright playoff slot. Ahead, 77-70, Pasig banked on Warlo Batac and Jerome Garcia to pull away, 97-75, midway through the final frame before coasting to its 10th win in 20 starts. Pasig is in seventh place in the North division and could still overtake Pasay and Meycauayan Marilao (12-10) for the sixth spot and an outright stint in the quarterfinal playoffs. Teams ranked seventh to 10th will have to go through the play-in, with the best two performers completing the playoff cast in both North and South divisions. Garcia, a homegrown icon, posted 28 points, 6 rebounds and 2 assists to edge Batac, with 26 points, 11 rebounds and 3 assists, for the best player accolade. Jerald Bautista supported with 15 points, 9 rebounds, 3 assists and 2 steals, followed by Jacob Galicia, with 9 points, 10 rebounds and 2 assists, and John Felix Corpuz, with 10 points and 2 rebounds. Also-ran Manila fell to a league-worst 1-22 slate despite Joe Gomez De Liano's 22 points, 9 rebounds, 2 assists and 2 steals; John Ashley Faa's 22 points, 8 rebounds, 5 assists and 3 steals; Alfred Sedillo's 16 points, 11 rebounds, 5 assists and 2 steals; and Mark Doligon's 10 points, 9 rebounds and 9 assists. The tournament returns to the Batangas City Coliseum on Wednesday, featuring games between Valenzuela and Rizal Province at 5 p.m., and San Juan and Batangas at 7 p.m.

‘Bawal ang Petiks’: Cainta mayor calls for serious TUPAD applicants. Cainta, Rizal Mayor Keith Nieto has encouraged residents seeking temporary employment to apply for the Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers (TUPAD) program, saying the opportunity is only for those who are genuinely willing to work. On Tuesday, Aug. 25, Nieto said the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) allocated funds for the program in Cainta, which will provide temporary employment to 80 residents. He said those selected for the program will work for 31 days, mainly along major waterways in Cainta, where they will help desilt box culverts and concrete pipes and clean cistern tanks to help clear clogged drainage systems. They will receive P600 per day, with Nieto reminding applicants, “Pero alam niyo naman, para ito sa mga gusto talaga ng trabaho, at may output ang programa natin (But as you know, this is for those who are genuinely willing to work, and our program has an expected output).” “Sa mga interesado, apply kayo sa akin… ulitin ko lang, seryosong trabaho ito… bawal ang petiks (For those who are interested, apply. Again, this is serious work—no slacking off),” he said. Nieto also thanked DOLE and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., assuring them that every peso allocated for the program would be used wisely to further improve the municipality. The TUPAD program recently drew attention after Malacañang called out some beneficiaries for allegedly posing as waterway cleaners in photos and videos while failing to perform the work they were hired to do. In a press briefing on Thursday, Aug. 13, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the reported fake photos and videos of TUPAD beneficiaries were particularly disappointing because they are paid to perform actual community work, including debris clearing and the declogging of canals. Castro said beneficiaries should fulfill their obligations instead of using government-funded work to produce what she described as fake videos, adding that the program was intended to provide temporary income while addressing community needs. TUPAD is the DOLE emergency employment program that provides temporary work to disadvantaged or displaced workers, including those who are underemployed, displaced, or affected by seasonal employment and other circumstances that disrupt their livelihood. It covers community-based work such as cleaning and maintaining public facilities, clearing debris, declogging canals, segregating waste, and clearing waterways, making it one of the government's mechanisms for providing short-term income while addressing local community needs. TUPAD beneficiaries are paid based on the prevailing minimum wage in their locality for the duration of their approved work, subject to program requirements and validated attendance. Alex Eala in awe of Federer comeback. Following her exit in the mixed doubles competition with Canadian partner Felix Auger-Aliassime, the 21-year-old Eala joined some of her fellow tennis stars in the stands, witnessing the comeback game of Federer against American rival Andy Roddick. “Enjoying a night full of legendary tennis!,” WTA wrote on its Instagram post with snaps of Eala during the red carpet.
