PLDT Enterprise brings Starlink support to Mindanao recovery efforts. In the aftermath of the powerful earthquake that struck parts of Mindanao, PLDT Enterprise, together with PLDT and Smart, deployed Starlink satellite connectivity solutions and mobilized emergency communications support to assist communities, responders and local government units in maintaining critical links during a time of urgent need. PLDT and Smart immediately dispatched field and operations teams to assess network facilities and support restoration activities in affected areas, including General Santos City and several municipalities in South Cotabato. This was made possible through close coordination among PLDT Enterprise, the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), and local government units on the ground. Assessments showed that most PLDT and Smart network facilities remained stable and operational, with service disruptions largely caused by commercial power interruptions affecting certain sites. PLDT Enterprise successfully rolled out Starlink connectivity solutions in areas where communications infrastructure had been affected, helping provide vital connectivity for emergency response operations and local communities. These deployments serviced impacted areas, including Malungon Sarangani Provincial Hospital and Alabel Sarangani Provincial Hospital, as well as command centers and rescue operation centers supporting emergency response and coordination efforts in affected areas. "During emergencies, connectivity becomes deeply personal. It allows people to reach loved ones, enables responders to coordinate more effectively and helps communities begin the difficult work of rebuilding," said Menardo “Butch" G. Jimenez Jr., Chief Operating Officer of PLDT. Support for the Front Lines of Disaster Response When and Where Communication Matters Most The deployment of Starlink solutions reflects PLDT Enterprise's broader commitment to delivering resilient and rapidly deployable connectivity to communities and institutions facing challenging circumstances, particularly in locations affected by disaster-related disruptions, power outages or geographic limitations. “We strive to be the first responders for the first responders because restoring connectivity at the front line of a disaster can be a powerful force multiplier,” said Blums Pineda, Senior Vice President and Head of Enterprise Business Group at PLDT Enterprise. “That means getting our response teams on the ground quickly to assess needs, restore services, and support connectivity where it matters most. The faster we reconnect communities and response teams, the sooner every call, every update, and every connection can help make a difference.” The initiative underscores the importance of dependable and flexible communications infrastructure in supporting disaster response and community resilience. Through solutions such as Starlink Satellite Broadband, PLDT Enterprise continues to equip local governments, emergency responders and institutions with technology that can help sustain communications when conventional networks face significant challenges. As Mindanao communities move forward from disaster response to rebuilding, PLDT Enterprise, PLDT, and Smart remain committed to working alongside local partners to support response and rebuilding efforts, ensuring that connectivity remains available when it matters most.

Ha Young gains 500,000 Instagram followers amid family controversy. Korean actress Ha Young has gained more than 500,000 followers on Instagram since the controversy over her great-grandfather’s alleged ties to Japan’s colonial rule erupted. Her growing social media following comes as her drama “Our Sticky Love,” co-starring Jung Hae-in, continues to perform well on Netflix. Based on Social Blade statistics, Ha Young’s Instagram followers increased by 514,375 from 845,203 on Aug. 7 to 1,359,578 on Aug. 25. The increase came after she appeared on the TV show “Problem Child in House” on Aug. 7 and talked about her great-grandfather. “My great-grandfather was the first doctor to open a practice in Hanyang after returning from Japan where he learned Western medicine. He also treated Emperor Gojong [ruler of Korea from 1864 to 1907] ,” she said. Her late great-grandfather, Ahn Sang-ho, was subsequently identified by Korean netizens as an alleged pro-Japanese collaborator during the period when Korea was under Japanese rule. Korea was annexed by Japan in 1910 and remained under Japanese rule for 35 years until 1945. Ha Young later apologized for her remarks. “Shamefully, in that state of ignorance, I spoke of my great-grandfather at various gatherings as if he were a source of family pride,” she said. She added that after doing her own research, she “discovered my great-grandfather's pro-Japanese activities.” Despite the controversy, Ha Young’s social media following has continued to climb. Meanwhile, “Our Sticky Love” has remained among Netflix’s global top 10 non-English shows for three consecutive weeks.

Liza Soberano honors Lea Salonga, Dolly de Leon as Filipino global trailblazers. Liza Soberano may be making her own mark internationally, but she is quick to acknowledge the Filipino artists who paved the way for talents like her to dream of making it big on the global stage. During a special media conference for her upcoming animated film "Forgotten Island" in Manila on Aug. 25, Liza expressed her gratitude to artists such as Lea Salonga and Dolly de Leon, whom she considers among those who helped open doors for the next generation of Filipino talent. "I feel very honored and proud. I don't necessarily feel I'm at the center of it. When I think about where I'm at right now, I'm just so grateful to be in the likes of Ms. Dolly and Ms. Lea, all of the people that've been paving the way for the longest time, so that I could be able to have this opportunity," Liza said. For Liza, the achievements of Lea and Dolly go beyond their individual careers. "All the work that they did in those times when it wasn't as easy made it easier for us to be here. I also like to honor those people who really tried to push the Filipino movement and culture forward," she added. Meanwhile, Liza, who made her Hollywood debut in the 2024 film "Lisa Frankenstein," said she never imagined in her wildest dreams that she would get the opportunity to work alongside talents such as Grammy-winning singer and actress H.E.R., "Forgotten Island" directors Januel Mercado and Joel Crawford, and fellow Filipino artists Lea and Dolly. "It feels like such a blessing to be part, even a small part, of that movement of bringing Filipino culture to the whole world," she said. The actress also sees "Forgotten Island" as another opportunity to bring Filipino culture and talent to a global audience. Directed by Mercado and Crawford, the DreamWorks Animation film follows high school graduates Jo and Raisa, best friends since grade school, who are transported to the magical island of Nakali, where they encounter creatures from Filipino mythology. Stepping into the shoes of Raisa Liza voices Raisa, a "Type A" friend who likes to stay organized. She admitted that portraying the character pushed her out of her comfort zone. "I think finding the right balance between being a child and being mature," Liza said when asked about the challenge of playing Raisa. "But also, just in terms of the emotional depth, too, because I've done a lot of dramatic acting here in the Philippines, and when it came to the drama of this film, I wanted to make sure that it was still rooted in light-hearted, almost childlike tampuhan and everything," she said. Liza also found a personal connection to Raisa's family dynamic, particularly her relationship with her grandmother. "The aspect of having Lola raise Jo and Liza is one of the things that instantly drew me to the project. I'm also a Lola and a Lola's girl. I grew up with my grandparents—they raised me. So I felt that family dynamic was very accurate. But almost every single scene has some sort of Easter egg," she shared. Apart from Liza, H.E.R., Lea and Dolly, "Forgotten Island" also features the voices of Dave Franco, Jenny Slate, Manny Jacinto, Jo Koy, and Ronny Chieng.

100 Years of Ducati, One Unforgettable Weekend. Text and photos by Zach Lucero Back in 2024, I was invited to cover the World Ducati Week (WDW) in Misano, Italy, an event that happens every 2 years where Ducati riders from across the planet converge. That gathering turned out to be a preshow for this year's WDW, which coincides with Ducati's 100th anniversary. Ducati was founded on July 4, 1926, in Bologna, Italy, by Industrialist and businessman Antonio Cavalieri Ducati and his three sons, Marcello, Bruno, and Adriano. Their actually started their business by manufacturing radio components and vacuum tubes before pivoting to motorcycles after World War II. Many motorcycle brands emerged after the war, as these two-wheelers became a practical and affordable mode of transportation in war-torn Europe at the time. 100 years of two-wheels One hundred years. I’m trying to wrap my head around the meaning of a brand being around this long. Obviously, Ducati’s resilience stems from its passion and commitment to building high-quality, high-performance motorcycles. Compared to previous years, this edition of World Ducati Week carried a slightly different tone. The event still had its trademark mix of speed, camaraderie, and good-natured hooliganism, but there was also an unmistakable sense of reverence. It reminded me of the quiet pride parents feel as they watch their child reach another defining milestone. Ducati's 100th year is not merely another corporate centenary. Plenty of brands can claim longevity. Ducati's legacy, however, has been built over a century of engineering high-performance motorcycles while amassing podium finishes, championship titles, and a level of racing success that has shaped the sport across generations. Ducatisti Our hotel was barely four kilometers from the Misano World Circuit. Under normal circumstances, the drive would have taken about 10 minutes. On World Ducati Week, it became a test of patience, stretching to nearly an hour and a half. By 7:00 a.m., the roads were already at a standstill as thousands of Ducatisti streamed in from every corner of the world. The anticipation was unmistakable. With every passing minute, the excitement intensified, reinforcing the idea that WDW is where Ducati's charisma is most vividly on display. Here, the brand is personified by its people. You see Ducati reflected in the the marquee’s fans—their energy, their passion, and their sense of camaraderie. The brand’s personality doesn't just live in its motorcycles; it comes alive in the people who ride them. Our days were packed with activities. We visited the 100,000-sq.m Ducati factory, experienced the Ducati museum tour, test-rode their new bikes, which included the new Ducati Desert X, Hypermotard and the Monster V2. There were also action-packed stunt rides, a Ducati parade, a beach party and of course, the highlight of World Ducati Week, The Race of Champions where Ducati MotoGP and World Superbike riders battled it out in an exhibition match for the fans. MotoGP This year's Race of Champions saw Nicolò Bulega, Álvaro Bautista, and Lorenzo Baldassarri claim the podium. Former MotoGP world champion Francesco Bagnaia finished fifth, while reigning MotoGP champion Marc Márquez crossed the line in 12th. Márquez in 12th may seem surprising at first glance, but the result needs context. As prestigious as the Race of Champions is, it remains an exhibition event. With the MotoGP and WorldSBK seasons still underway, factory riders have little incentive to take unnecessary risks. The goal is to put on a great show while avoiding the kind of crash or injury that could compromise their championship campaigns. Ducati CEO One of the highlights of the trip was the opportunity to spend some one-on-one time with Ducati CEO Claudio Domenicali, the man who has led the company to unprecedented success. I first met him two years ago and immediately understood why he commands such respect throughout Ducati. He is thoughtful, technically astute, and carries himself with a quiet confidence that inspires trust. I was particularly keen to discuss Ducati's electric sportbike project with Domenicali. He explained that the biggest hurdle remains the battery, as current technology still falls short of Ducati's performance standards. Rather than develop its own batteries, Ducati is working closely with suppliers, pushing them to create a power source worthy of the brand. For now, I don't see Ducati rushing into electrification. As the benchmark in high-performance internal combustion motorcycles, it has little reason to move until battery technology can truly deliver the performance and emotion riders expect from a Ducati. World Ducati Week 2026 was a fitting celebration of Ducati's first century—a brand built on innovation, racing success, and uncompromising performance. Here's to the next hundred years. Salute. Forza Ducati.

Mayor Isko orders door-to-door anti-leptospirosis drive as Manila cases surge. Manila City Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno” Domagoso ordered health workers to conduct door-to-door visits as part of an intensified campaign against leptospirosis following a sharp rise in cases in the city. Domagoso issued the directive on Wednesday, Aug. 26, after meeting with officer‑in‑charge City Health Officer Dr. Grace Padilla and directors of the city’s seven district hospitals to discuss the rise in infections following flooding caused by the southwest monsoon (Habagat). “Ibaliktad natin 'yung sitwasyon: na hindi na tayo ang hanapin, tayo na ang humanap sa mga posibleng na-expose sa baha at nakararamdam ng ilang sintomas ng impeksyon ng leptospirosis (Let us reverse the situation. Instead of waiting for people to come to us, we should look for those who may have been exposed to floodwaters and are experiencing symptoms of leptospirosis),” Domagoso said during his livestream. According to the Manila Public Information Office, the city recorded 89 new leptospirosis cases on Aug. 26, 38 on Aug. 25, 16 on Aug. 24, 10 on Aug. 23, 11 on Aug. 22, 22 on Aug. 21, and 11 on Aug. 20. This brought the total number of new cases recorded during the week to 197. Five patients also died from leptospirosis during the same period, including one on Aug. 24, two on Aug. 25, and two on Aug. 26. “Ako ay taos-pusong nakikiramay sa limang pamilya ng mga sumakabilang-buhay ito lamang pong linggong ito (I extend my deepest condolences to the families of the five people who died this week),” the mayor said. Domagoso warned that cases may continue to rise because of the disease’s incubation period, noting that residents exposed to floodwaters during the Aug. 17 to 18 habagat may only now begin showing symptoms. “Patuloy pa itong lalaki. Posibleng lumaki kung ganito ang escalation, nahihinog pa lang ho ang impeksyon (The number may continue to increase. If this trend continues, more cases may still emerge because the infection is only beginning to develop),” he said. The mayor said the city currently has 389,000 doxycycline capsules available across its health facilities, up from 51,000 remaining capsules as of Aug. 24. Of the additional supply, 300,000 capsules came from the Department of Health, while 40,000 were donated by the private sector. “Sa mga taga-lungsod ng Maynila, mahirap, middle class, mayaman, meron po tayo at pwede niyong ma-access yung 389,000 doxycycline capsules (For residents of Manila, whether poor, middle class, or wealthy, we have 389,000 doxycycline capsules available and accessible to you),” Domagoso said. He urged residents exposed to floodwaters to visit any of Manila’s 44 health centers or seven district hospitals for free consultation and appropriate preventive treatment, even if they have yet to develop symptoms. Domagoso also raised concern over congestion at the Ospital ng Maynila Medical Center, where 69 patients were being accommodated in its 40-bed emergency room as of Wednesday morning. “Kahit gaano kalaki yung emergency room ng Ospital ng Maynila, I can honestly say that our situation is we are now being overwhelmed by the infection ng ating mga pasyente na infected ng leptospirosis (No matter how large the emergency room of Ospital ng Maynila is, I can honestly say that we are now being overwhelmed by the number of patients infected with leptospirosis),” he said. The Ospital ng Maynila Medical Center earlier reported that its emergency room had reached 300 percent capacity over the past two days amid a surge in patients, including suspected and confirmed leptospirosis cases. READ: https://mb.com.ph/2026/08/26/ospital-ng-maynila-er-reaches-300-capacity To help decongest emergency rooms, the city activated the Manila Infectious Disease Control Center at Santa Ana Hospital, which has 17 beds for leptospirosis patients. Ten beds were already occupied as of Wednesday. Domagoso also ordered the opening of additional wards in other city hospitals to accommodate more patients. He advised residents to watch for early symptoms such as fever, severe headache, muscle pain, and reddening of the eyes, and to seek medical attention immediately instead of self-medicating. “Huwag niyong panghinayangan yung kikitain natin sa pagpasok sa trabaho, kasi pera lang yan. Balewala po lahat yan pagka huli na ang lahat (Do not worry about the income you might lose by missing work. Money can be earned again, but it will mean nothing if it is already too late),” Domagoso said.

BIR gambling crackdown: 11 ‘sabongan’ raided over unrecorded machines. The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) launched simultaneous enforcement operations targeting 11 cockpit arenas, part of an expanding nationwide drive to force unregulated gambling technology into compliance. During the Aug. 8 raids, the BIR said revenue enforcement officers uncovered 297 unrecorded betting machines, computerized betting units, servers, and related electronic devices operating without the required Permit to Use (PTU). BIR agents, supported by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), systematically sealed or confiscated the hardware in accordance with existing tax regulations. The coordinated crackdown covered venues in Metro Manila and South Luzon following covert verification operations conducted by BIR Revenue Regions. The crackdown comes amid growing scrutiny from tax authorities over computerized betting equipment in traditional venues. BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza stressed that arena operators must strictly comply with official accounting standards. “Betting transactions must be properly recorded, and the machines used for them must be properly registered with the BIR,” Mendoza said in a statement. “We will continue checking cockpit operations nationwide and take appropriate action when we find violations,” he added. The regulatory offensive has already triggered initial compliance measures from affected establishments. Following the raids, several venue operators initiated procedures to register previously off-the-books hardware while settling back taxes and accrued penalties to secure the unsealing or release of their equipment. Concurrently, BIR auditors are reviewing machine log files and electronic transaction records to quantify historical betting volume and determine whether additional tax liabilities exist. Mendoza confirmed that the enforcement campaign will broaden across the country. He directed all Revenue Regions and Revenue District Offices to map, audit, and verify every active arena operating within their jurisdictions. The agency emphasized that its approach prioritizes voluntary compliance, offering technical assistance to venue operators seeking to rectify registration deficits before strict sanctions apply. Operators that fail to voluntarily update their registration status and settle outstanding liabilities will face formal administrative and enforcement proceedings.

Marcos transfers administrative supervision of PCUP, NAPC to Malacañang. President Marcos has transferred the administrative supervision of the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor (PCUP) and the National Anti-Poverty Commission (NAPC) to the Office of the President, bringing the two agencies back under direct Palace oversight. The transfer was ordered under Executive Order (EO) No. 123, signed by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto on Aug. 18, 2026. The order said placing the PCUP and NAPC under the administrative supervision of the Office of the President would strengthen policy coordination, ensure greater convergence of poverty reduction and urban development initiatives, and facilitate the implementation of programs requiring a whole-of-government approach. The PCUP was created under EO No. 82 issued in 1986 and was placed under the Office of the President to serve as a direct link between the urban poor and the government in policy formulation and program implementation. The NAPC, meanwhile, was created under Republic Act No. 8425, or the Social Reform and Poverty Alleviation Act, as a coordinating and advisory body for the implementation of the Social Reform Agenda and the government's poverty alleviation and reduction programs. Executive Order No. 67, issued in 2018, had transferred the administrative supervision of both agencies to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) to harmonize their policies and programs with the department's poverty alleviation and social services initiatives. The new order cited EO No. 72 issued in 2002, which provides that agencies whose mandates or functions require the immediate attention of the President and cut across different sectors should be placed under the Office of the President.

PFF World Cup hosting takes center stage at Sports Tourism Awards. The Philippine Football Federation (PFF) emerged as the biggest winner at the 7th Philippine Sports Tourism Awards after clinching two major honors— National Sports Association of the Year and International Event of the Year — for its successful hosting of the FIFA Futsal Women’s World Cup at the Philsports Arena. Under the leadership of its president John Gutierrez, the twin victories underscored how the PFF’s trailblazing event served as a powerful showcase of sports tourism that elevated destinations, inspired communities and placed the country firmly on the global sporting map. PSC Chairman Patrick Gregorio, guest of honor at the awards night, praised the federation’s achievement. ``The FIFA Futsal Women’s World Cup was a celebration of how sports can bring nations together and put the Philippines on the global map,’’ said Gregorio, noting that the event exemplified the synergy between tourism and athletic development. The awards night itself, organized by the Sports Tourismo Alliance Committee and presented by the Philippine Sports Commission, highlighted the diverse ways sports tourism is flourishing nationwide. World Archery Philippines was named Emerging NSA of the Year, while the Tour of Luzon earned Domestic Event of the Year. The City of Puerto Princesa and Sunrise Events were honored as Event Organizers of the Year, with Puerto Princesa also recognized as Emerging Destination of the Year and the City of Lapu-Lapu cited for Destination Marketing Event of the Year. As the Chairperson of the National Sports Tourism Inter-Agency Committee (NST-IAC), Gregorio commended the honorees for their excellence and persistence in advancing athletic excellence while also highlighting the country's top destinations on the global stage. “We all believe that the biggest tourism events in the world are sports events. Napaka-swerte natin dahil President Marcos really believes that sports tourism is a strategy not only to promote tourism but to develop grassroots sports,” said Gregorio. He cited the just-concluded 4th Southeast Asia Open Water Swimming Championships in Boracay and the recent Aerobic Gymnastics Asian Championships, the Tour of Luzon as examples of how hosting boosts local participation and global exposure and underscored the transformative power of sports tourism. Industry partners were likewise celebrated: Duck Sports as Media Outfit of the Year, Grand Country Tour and Travel as Tour Operator of the Year, Marriott Charity Golf as Charity Event of the Year, New Clark City as Venue of the Year, and Philippine Airlines as Airline of the Year. Hospitality and events were represented by NUSTAR Resort Cebu (Hotel of the Year) and the Sports Tourism Forum at SMX Clark (M.I.C.E Event of the Year). The evening also paid tribute to Charles Lim of the Sports Tourismo Alliance Committee, whose leadership has steered the awards since inception. “What is unique with sports tourism is that while athletes compete for points and prize money, the host country showcases its destinations to millions of viewers worldwide,’’ said Gregorio. ``From tennis to surfing, cycling to futsal, sambo to karate, these events bring athletes, fans, and federations together and in the process, they elevate the Philippines on the global sports map,” added Gregorio. The Subic Bay Freeport Zone was named Destination of the Year, veteran sports leader Cynthia Carrion was honored as Sports Personality of the Year, and the Island Living Channel was recognized as Local TV Sports Media Outfit of the Year. Also present during the awarding ceremony were SBMA Chairman and Administrator Eduardo Jose Alino and Atty. Agnes Devanadera, President and CEO of Clark Development Corporation as special guests and awardees together with Philippine Retirement Authority General Manager and Chief Executive Officer Roberto ``Bob’’ Zozobrado. By bringing the world’s best women’s futsal teams to Manila, the PFF not only showcased the country’s organizational capacity but also generated a ripple effect across tourism and grassroots sports. Hotels, restaurants, and transport services benefited from the influx of athletes, officials, and fans, while young Filipino players gained invaluable exposure by competing on home soil. “When we host events of this magnitude, we don’t just welcome athletes and fans. we showcase our destinations, inspire our youth, and strengthen our national identity through sports,’’ said Gregorio. The country will host the biggest surfing event on the planet on October 31 to November 10—the World Surf League Championship Tour where the top 40 surfers in the world will see action while the Asian U19 Sepak Takraw Championships (Nov. 18-25) and the East Asia Baseball Cup (Nov. 26-Dec. 5) are likewise on the pipeline.

Vlogger, live-in partner fall in Negros drug bust. Agents of the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) arrested on Tuesday, Aug. 25, a vlogger and his live-in partner during a buy-bust operation in Bacolod City. In a statement, the PDEA said content creator Joselito Peruelo and companion Christian Tolentino were collared at around 3 p.m. following the operation in Purok Magtiayon, Barangay 10. Following information from tipsters, the PDEA-Negros Island Region operatives pounced on the couple immediately after an undercover agent signalled that the deal was consummated. During the search, the PDEA agents seized around 50 grams of suspected shabu worth more than P340,000 from the seemingly shocked couple. The suspects are now in PDEA custody and will face charges for violation of the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act.

SB19’s Justin recalls being called ‘suplado’ by Filipino airport worker in LA. SB19 member Justin De Dios recalled an uncomfortable encounter with a Filipino airport employee in Los Angeles, saying he found the man's comments toward the group's manager disrespectful. Justin talked about the incident in SB19's latest YouTube vlog, recalling what happened after the group landed in LA and was waiting to collect their luggage. The situation began when an elderly Filipino woman approached the group and asked for photos. According to Justin, manager Leah Gonzales politely asked the woman to wait until the members had finished getting their bags. The woman eventually got her photos with the members once they were free. It was what happened afterward that bothered Justin. He said an airport employee who had overheard Leah's request approached her and asked for her name before telling her, "Suplada ka, ah." Justin questioned why the employee reacted that way when Leah had not been speaking to him in the first place. "Maayos naman 'yung pagkakasabi nung manager namin, tapos hindi naman siya 'yung kausap. Na-overheard lang... hindi naman technically pinipigilan, nakapagpa-picture na nga eh," he said. Justin said the employee did not stop there. He recalled that the man continued making remarks about Leah and the group, including questioning why SB19 members would not immediately pose for photos with people who approached them. Among the comments Justin remembered was, "Di pa nga sikat, 'di na nagpapa-picture." The employee also reportedly talked about his own encounters with celebrities and showed photos of himself with famous personalities, according to Justin. Rather than immediately responding, Justin said he tried to understand what the employee was saying before deciding whether to confront him. "Si kuya na nagwo-work doon sa airport, bakit siya nagre-react ng ganon? Ako ang ginagawa ko nung time na 'yun, pinapakinggan ko siya maigi kung ano 'yung point niya," Justin recalled. He eventually decided against escalating the situation. "But the thing is... parang ang hirap lang gumalaw kasi parang siyempre delikado and all, pero talagang as in super disrespectful," he said. The encounter continued when the employee approached Justin directly and asked if he was part of SB19. Justin also recalled the man pointing out fans waiting outside the airport. At one point, the employee reportedly called the fans through a video call and showed them on his phone. Justin said he and the rest of the group, along with Leah, ultimately chose not to engage further. For him, the incident was particularly uncomfortable because the person involved was also Filipino. "Well, sa mga past tours naman namin, hindi naman ganon 'yung na-experience namin. Pero like sa Filipino pa namin mae-experience 'yung ganon. Tapos parang, it's very normal sa kanila. Tapos parang kami pa 'yung mali," Justin said. He ended his recollection with a sarcastic remark about the group's arrival in Los Angeles. "Grabe, wow, the welcome committee sa pag-land ng LA... Shoutout to you, kuya!" he said.

License alone no guarantee of higher pay for education graduates—PIDS. Having a professional license improves the employment prospects of education graduates in the Philippines, but does not necessarily translate into higher wages unless paired with public-sector employment and jobs aligned with their training, according to state-run policy think tank Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS). In a discussion paper published last Tuesday, Aug. 25, PIDS researchers found that while licensure serves as an important signal of professional skills and competence, its labor market benefits are not guaranteed and largely depend on where graduates work. The paper, titled “Labor Market Outcomes of Education Graduates in the Philippines: The Role of Licensure Credentials and Job Matching,” was authored by PIDS research specialist Anna Rita P. Vargas, research analyst Paola Ellaine D. Luzon, and senior research fellow Connie G. Bayudan-Dacuycuy. Using data from the July 2024 round of the merged labor force survey-annual poverty indicators survey (LFS-APIS), the study examined whether professional licensing translates into advantages in employment, job quality, and remuneration among education science and related program graduates. Nine out of 10 licensed graduates were participating in the labor market, 22 percentage points (ppts) higher than the 68 percent among their unlicensed counterparts. Licensed graduates also had a higher share of employed workers at 84 percent, compared with 54 percent among those without licenses. However, the researchers found that licensure alone did not significantly raise wages. “Earnings of education graduates are driven less by licensure alone and more by how their credentials interact with class of work, specifically whether the graduate is employed in the public sector,” the study said. Education-occupation matching significantly increased wages, while the highest wage returns were recorded when graduates were both professionally licensed and employed by the government or government-owned and/or -controlled corporations (GOCCs). Job matching also improved employment quality among licensed graduates, with those working in education-related jobs having a 7.2-percent probability of underemployment, lower than the 8.46 percent among those working outside the sector. Licensed graduates in public employment had an even lower 3.98-percent probability of underemployment, compared with 14.73 percent among those in the private sector or self-employed. Based on the findings, the researchers called for well-defined career pathways for education graduates to improve job matching in both licensure and non-licensure programs and better align employment opportunities with their skills and training. The study also urged the Commission on Higher Education (CHED), the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), and the Department of Education (DepEd) to regularly review the alignment of teacher education programs, licensure examination competencies, and labor market needs. The researchers recommended targeted capacity-building for higher education institutions (HEIs) with consistently weak licensure examination performance, as well as structured licensure preparation and assistance for graduates at risk of not passing the examination. They also proposed expanding financial support for aspiring licensed professionals, noting that the Unified Student Financial Assistance System for Tertiary Education (UniFAST) currently provides its grantees with a one-time ₱8,000 reimbursement for taking board or licensure examinations. The researchers further called for the integration of licensure, education, and employment data into national labor market information systems to strengthen teacher deployment, career placement, and coordination between higher education institutions and employers. - Danielle T. Bayani

Prosecutor Ligutan stands by viral Facebook post, says 'teacher's instinct kicked in'. Private prosecutor Amando Virgil Ligutan insisted on proprietary of his Facebook post two weeks ago, even as it ultimately became the reason why the Senate impeachment court laid down stricter rules on public statements by the parties in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial. “Correcting a mistake is never wrong. Doing it while a hearing is on-going, online, does not make it not right. Ang pagtatama ng mali ay kailanman hindi ipinagbabawal. Kahit sa loob ng impeachment court na ito,” Ligutan said in a manifestation in open court Wednesday morning, Aug. 26. (Correcting what is wrong is never prohibited, even within this impeachment court.) Ligutan was referring to his Facebook post during the Aug. 12 impeachment hearing wherein he assailed the notion that misleading questions were allowed during a witness' cross-examination. This post would later be called out by Duterte’s defense team before presiding officer Senator Francis "Chiz" Escudero. Proud teacher Ligutan--who described himself as a proud teacher--says he simply can't let such remarks go uncorrected. “That’s why I made that post. I was concerned that the statement made in open court — that misleading questions are allowed — will go unchecked. My teacher’s instinct kicked in,” Ligutan said. Ligutan said he has practiced law for almost 16 years but has been a teacher and educator for nearly 20. "First and foremost I am a teacher. Isa po akong guro. Usa ko ka maestro (I am a teacher). And I am proud to be one,” he said. The Cebuano underscored: “Ang pagtuturo, ang pagtatama ng mali, ay walang pinipiling lugar, at walang pinipiling panahon.” (Teaching and correcting what is wrong have no specific place and no specific time.) The dispute originated from an exchange between prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan and defense counsel Kristine Ferrer during the Aug. 12 proceedings. Kapunan initially referred to "leading questions" before correcting herself to "misleading questions". Ferrer responded that “they are allowed,” an exchange that Ligutan said prompted concern among members of the legal community. That's why he posted: “A principle ALL lawyers and law students know by heart: Misleading questions are NOT allowed even on cross-examination.” However, Ligutan denied that the viral post was directed to any member of the defense. “To the defense, the post is not about you. It is not personal. It is about the law that we all adhere to,” he said. Ligutan also maintained that the post did not touch on respondent Duterte’s liability or the evidence being heard by the impeachment court. “But what did I violate? I did not discuss the merits of the case. I did not discuss the strength or weakness of the legal arguments or evidence of either side," he explained. According to the prosecutor, he merely stated a procedural rule without identifying anyone or commenting on the substance of the impeachment charge. “Your honors, we in the prosecution panel also have rights. I, for one, did not surrender my freedom to teach and to enlighten, when I decided to participate in this trial,” Ligutan said. “Patuloy po akong magiging guro kahit sa loob ng impeachment court na ito,” he vowed. (I will continue to be a teacher even inside this impeachment court.)

Gilas coach Tim Cone is a big Alex Eala fan. A blown chance for Gilas Pilipinas head coach Tim Cone three years ago may yet find fulfillment at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya next month. Unless destiny intervenes—again. Cone had it all planned during the 19th edition of the Asian Games in Hangzhou in 2023: find a break in the schedule of the men’s basketball competition and go off to watch Alex Eala in action. Yes, Alex Eala, now the rising star of women’s tennis, but still two years away at the time from her breakthrough tournament at the Miami Open. With Gilas having blitzed Bahrain and Thailand in the group phase in late September that year, a victory over Jordan and PBA import Rondae Hollis-Jefferson in the next game would have sent the Philippines to the quarterfinals outright on Oct. 3 against Iran, leaving Oct. 1 and 2 open for a quick side trip for Cone to the Hangzhou Olympic Expo Center, which housed the tennis matches. But fate intervened. Behind RHJ’s 24 points, Jordan crushed the Philippines, 87-62, leaving Cone incommunicado to everyone else except team manager Alfrancis Chua during the long walk from the gymnasium back to where the bus was parked, and all the way to the hotel. Thrown into a hellish sudden-death game against Qatar, Cone pulled out all the stops and dragged everybody to the practice venue the next day to prepare for the game that mattered most at that point. Fueled by the frightening thought of going home empty-handed, the Philippines came out blazing and annihilated Qatar, 80-41, advancing to the quarterfinals, where it shocked Iran by one point. That set the stage for the unforgettable comeback against China in the semifinals, followed by a masterful revenge victory over Jordan in the final. Lost for Cone, a tennis buff, however, in the dizzying run to a gold-medal finish—a first for the country in the Asiad since 1962—was the opportunity to cheer for Eala as she battled some of the region’s best women players. Three years later, Cone still remembers the details clearly. “If we had beaten Jordan, we would have had a day break and gone straight to the quarters. But by losing, we had to do a playoff against Qatar to make it to the quarters,” Cone said on Viber. “Because we lost [to Jordan], our next game was scheduled at the same time as her match. I was disappointed not to watch because I'm a big tennis fan.” Now comes the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games next month, with Gilas Pilipinas and Cone bracketed with China, Bahrain and Kazakhstan in Group C as they bid to defend the title. Eala, who reached the semifinals and took the bronze in Hangzhou, has also recently confirmed her presence in the Games. Cone is thrilled at the prospect of finally getting to see the 21-year-old tennis phenom competing after missing out on a golden opportunity three years ago. “It would be awesome to watch Alex this time in Nagoya, if there's a chance,” said Cone, who a few days ago met two of Eala’s would-be teammates in Japan, Tenielle Madis and Stefi Aludo, at the Alabang Tennis Courts. “Looking forward to watching them,” Cone said. Hoping fate doesn’t have other plans this time.

CIDG arrests female fire officer in 'slot for sale' scheme in BFP. Operatives of the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) arrested a female personnel of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) for allegedly offering a slot to applicants in exchange for a huge sum of money. CIDG director Maj. Gen. Robert Alexander Morico said a surveillance operation was immediately conducted after they obtained a report of the alleged slot for sale scheme for applicants aspiring to become firemen. Based on the initial investigation, the female BFP personnel used a dummy account on Facebook messenger to negotiate the deal for a sure slot to the agency. “The suspect promised and gave a guarantee to facilitate his entry into the bureau in exchange for P500,000,” said Morico, adding that the revelation came from one of the applicants. During the initial meeting, the suspect presented her BFP identification card to the applicant and assured him that she has already facilitated similar transactions in the past —from applicants from other places including Laguna. The BFP female personnel then allegedly instructed the complainant to hand over the full amount P500,000 on Aug. 24 but the latter managed to negotiate an initial down payment of P300,000. It was then that the operation was carried out in Barangay Maimpis in San Fernando City at around 7 p.m. Aug. 24. “The suspect was caught red-handed while receiving the marked money from the applicant,” said Morico. Meanwhile, the BFP leadership vowed to investigate the incident as it stressed that the hiring process in the agency is strictly based on merit and physical and mental fitness. “We do not tolerate corruption within our ranks. Continuously working with the PNP, we will ensure anyone who exploits our aspiring applicants will face the law,” Kwan Tiu said. “We will hold our personnel accountable for their actions,” he added.
